findings.evidence: "The branch managers' working group audits renewal rates on the first of every month... The consortium's circulation team reviews monthly checkout volume after each fiscal period."
findings.fix: Either supply the actual renewal-rate/checkout-volume data and tie it explicitly to the fines argument, or remove the section.
findings.violation: This section describes monitoring processes but presents no actual figures, and neither renewal rates nor checkout volume are referenced anywhere else in the document to support the recommendation. It reads as disconnected filler.

findings.fix: Confirm the correct branch count and use it consistently throughout the document.
findings.violation: This contradicts "the four pilot branches absorbed the loss" in the "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section - the number of pilot branches is given as both 5 and 4.

findings.evidence: "the on-time-or-eventual return rate for borrowed items held at 94 percent, compared with 87 percent at the branches that kept fines in place over the same period"
findings.fix: Note how comparison branches were selected and whether they were matched to pilot branches on relevant characteristics, or qualify the finding as correlational.
findings.violation: The comparison branches were not randomly assigned and may differ from pilot branches in ways (patron demographics, staffing, collection size) that also affect return rates, so the gap is presented as if fines-removal caused it without ruling out confounds.

findings.evidence: "The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.fix: Either correct the pilot length to match the survey timing or explain why the survey was not administered at the pilot's actual conclusion.
findings.violation: The pilot is described as 16 months long, but the survey's second administration was at month 12, leaving the final four months of the pilot unmeasured and creating an unexplained mismatch with the stated pilot duration.

findings.evidence: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches"
findings.fix: Add justification for generalizing pilot results to the other five-plus branches, or scope the recommendation to branches with characteristics similar to the pilot set.
findings.violation: The pilot covered only 5 (or 4) of the 10 branches, yet the recommendation extrapolates to all ten without addressing whether the untested branches are comparable to the pilot branches.

findings.evidence: "replacing the current fine notices with automatic email reminders sent three, seven, and fourteen days after the due date"
findings.fix: State whether this reminder schedule was used in the pilot; if not, clarify it is a new, untested design choice.
findings.violation: This specific reminder schedule is introduced with no indication it was part of the pilot that produced the cited 94%/87% and survey results, so the evidence doesn't support this particular implementation detail.

findings.evidence: "matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established"
findings.fix: Either present the pilot data broken out by return-time window (showing the basis for the 60-day cutoff) or remove the claim that this threshold matches established pilot data.
findings.violation: No earlier part of the document describes the pilot measuring returns within a 60-day window; the "on-time-or-eventual return rate" figure given earlier has no stated timeframe, so this claim asserts a specific data pattern that was never shown.

findings.evidence: "Removing the financial penalty for late returns predictably increases both on-time return rates and overall program participation, which is the reason the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results... support ending fines for the whole consortium"
findings.fix: Replace the assertion with an actual argument for generalizability (e.g., similarity of untested branches to pilot branches, or a mechanism-based explanation independent of the conclusion it's meant to support).
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section
findings.violation: This is circular - it asserts the causal mechanism as self-evidently true and then uses that assertion as the reason the pilot data generalizes, rather than independently establishing causation or addressing scale-up risk.

findings.evidence: "This relationship is documented in the Tri-County Library Data Cooperative's 2023 fines-elimination research brief, which reviewed return-rate data from fourteen library systems that eliminated fines between 2017 and 2022."
findings.fix: Summarize the brief's relevant findings and explain why those fourteen systems are comparable to this consortium's branches.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section
findings.violation: This external study is cited without any detail on how comparable those fourteen systems are to this consortium (size, patron base, fine structure), so it doesn't actually substantiate the systemwide-generalization claim.

findings.evidence: "the four pilot branches absorbed the loss without a measurable change to their replacement-copy spending"
findings.fix: Provide consortium-wide revenue projections for all ten branches, or explicitly caveat that the no-shortfall finding is based only on the pilot subset.
findings.violation: Beyond the branch-count inconsistency noted above, this generalizes a revenue-neutral result from a handful of pilot branches to all ten branches without evidence that revenue loss scales the same way consortium-wide.
